title: How many whole units does five halves contain?
description: Five halves is written as five halves added together. The board groups the halves in twos to make whole units and finds one half left over. Keeko ties the answer to rotis cut into halves.
teaching_notes: One idea: the whole units in a fraction are the full groups of the bottom number in the top number, and the rest is the fractional part. Watch for students who forget the half left over.

source: How many whole units does 5/2 contain?
video_script.why: A learner finds the whole units inside five halves by grouping the halves in twos.
video_script.substitution: the book's own fraction five halves
video_script.anchor: five half-unit bars on a number line from 0 to 3
video_script.payoff_line: Five halves contains two whole units

final_answer.spoken: five halves contains two whole units, with one half left over

maths_rules: 5/2 means 5 parts, each 1/2 of a unit
2 halves make 1 whole, so 4 halves make 2 wholes
video_script.design: Five half-unit bars on the number line from zero. They join in twos into two whole bars and one half stays alone. Rotis cut into halves close the video.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; a number line from 0 to 3 with each unit cut into two parts; the black line of 5/2 from 0

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.line: the number line appears with each unit cut into two equal parts
marks.black: the black line of five halves is drawn from zero and passes the mark two

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book, and it uses a number line.
<bookmark mark='line'/>Each unit on this number line is cut into two equal parts.
<bookmark mark='black'/>The black line is five halves long and passes the mark two.
How many whole units does five halves contain?

beats.on_screen: the number line and the black line stay; the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: the fraction 5/2 shown as five half bars; a whole unit bar beside them

marks.means: five half bars of equal size line up from zero
marks.whole: a whole unit bar is shown beside them, as long as two half bars

narration: <bookmark mark='means'/>Five halves means five parts, and each part is one half of a unit.
<bookmark mark='whole'/>A whole unit is the same length as two of those halves.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the fraction that we have to look at is five halves.

beats.on_screen: To find: how many whole units 5/2 contains
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find how many whole units this fraction contains, and what is left.

marks.split: five halves is written as five halves added together

narration: <bookmark mark='split'/>Step one, write five halves as five halves added together. That is five times one half, as the book shows.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: 2 halves make 1 whole, so 4 halves make 2 wholes

marks.first: the first two half bars join into one whole unit bar
marks.second: the next two half bars join into a second whole unit bar

beats.colours: each pair of halves = its own colour
narration: <bookmark mark='first'/>Step two, two halves make one whole. The first two halves join to make one whole unit.
<bookmark mark='second'/>The next two halves make a second whole unit. Four halves make two wholes.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: one half is left over

marks.left: the fifth half bar stays alone, after the two whole units

narration: <bookmark mark='left'/>Step three, the fifth half cannot make another whole unit by itself. One half is left over.

beats.on_screen: Check: 4 halves + 1 half = 5 halves, the same as 5/2

marks.check: the two whole units and the left over half are put back together as five halves

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>To check, put all the pieces back together. Four halves and one half make five halves again.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Five halves contains two whole units.
It also has one more half left over after those two whole units.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the number line
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: five half rotis on a plate; two pairs join into two whole rotis and one half roti stays alone

marks.rotis: five half rotis appear on a plate
marks.join: two pairs of halves join into two whole rotis, and one half roti stays alone

narration: <bookmark mark='rotis'/>Think of the rotis in your book, each cut into two equal halves. Take five of those halves.
<bookmark mark='join'/>Put the halves together in pairs. You get two whole rotis and half a roti more.
